last_amend_reason:
ESC-029, GRANTED BY HANK IN SESSION 2026-09-05: "Let's go with your recommendation." Amends the FIXTURES of two frozen acceptance files so their inputs are complete under T-306's rule. NOT ONE ASSERTION WAS CHANGED, and that is proven mechanically rather than claimed: every line matching the assert-statement pattern is byte-identical before and after in test_e1_foundation.py, and every removed line in that file's diff is a validate_bid CALL SITE. In test_e4_store_agent.py nothing was removed at all -- one helper was added and one kwarg threaded through an existing dict.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Measured both directions on the same two files minutes apart: main 30 passed; branch task/money-path 11 failed, 19 passed (7 in E4, 4 in E1 -- so it moved the E1 pass rate as well as E4). Cause: grep list_prices in both files returned ZERO. They call the boundary with no roster at all. Under the old rule an absent roster meant "abstain", so the price wall stayed silent and each test measured its own subject -- provenance flagging, nonce replay, key rotation, the freshness window, expiry, blacklisting. T-306's whole content is that the absent roster must instead REFUSE, because a signed bid awarding itself 85% off was ACCEPTED whenever list_prices was omitted. So the wall began firing first and these tests never reached what they grade. Every one of the 11 failures was an `ok is True` CONTROL -- the half of each test that exists so it cannot pass by rejecting everything.

THE REPAIR, and why it is input completion rather than goal loosening. E1: one module-level _FIXTURE_ROSTER pricing prod-1 at the 49.00 the offer itself carries, with a 25% ceiling deeper than the 10% the offer declares, threaded into the 9 validate_bid call sites inside the 4 affected tests and nowhere else. The roster AGREES with the fixture, so it is not a second contradicting wall. E4: a _roster_for(payload) helper on the single shared _present door helper, DERIVED FROM THE PAYLOAD rather than hard-coded -- _external_payload takes unit_price as a parameter and callers vary it, so a fixed roster would be dishonest for any test passing a different price, and dishonest in the refusing direction. It is applied BEFORE kwargs.update(extra), so any test wanting to exercise the price wall itself can still pass an explicit list_prices= and win.

THIS MAKES THE GATE STRICTER, NOT LOOSER. The 85%-off admission stops being accepted anywhere, which is the entire point of T-306. What these 11 tests grade is unchanged; they simply stop being refused by a wall they were never written to exercise.

MEASURED AFTER, on main: the same two files give 30 passed -- identical to before the amendment -- so the arming is neutral on pre-T-306 behaviour and cannot be masking anything today. The decisive re-measurement against the T-306 branch follows this amendment.

THE SAME SHAPE WAS ALREADY REPAIRED IN NON-FROZEN CODE, which is the precedent: the money-path lane armed 70 dual-path tests the identical way, completing inputs and loosening nothing, and it separately proved that three OTHER xfail tests were XPASSing coincidentally on the same list_price_unavailable refusal -- removing those markers would have false-closed three open tickets. That is the same class of collateral, caught the same way.

RECORDED AS NOT VERIFIED at escalation time and still worth stating: I did not check whether any of the 11 asserts something about PRICING deliberately, in which case that one would be a genuine contradiction rather than an incomplete input. The post-amendment run against the T-306 branch is what settles it, and if any of the 11 fails there for a price reason it will be reported rather than re-armed.
